BPR-max uses per-example loss L = −log(Σⱼ sⱼ σ(rᵢ−rⱼ) + 10⁻²⁴) + λΣⱼ sⱼrⱼ², where s = softmax over negative scores only. It is the negative log of a weighted probability sum, not a weighted sum of log probabilities. Score regularization acts on negative scores, not model parameters. The official implementation differentiates through the softmax weights in both terms; do not detach them. Its PyTorch implementation optionally applies ELU before computing the entire objective, then sums examples; the original Theano implementation averages examples. [Official PyTorch loss implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py).

Sampling combines other minibatch targets with an additional shared pool drawn independently with replacement, with probability proportional to training interaction count raised to sample_alpha; 0 gives uniform sampling, 1 popularity sampling. The code concatenates targets and extra samples without deduplication. Only each row’s diagonal target occurrence is excluded from its negative softmax: duplicate target IDs elsewhere remain, including accidental positive collisions. Thus masking every matching positive ID would be a deliberate change from the official objective. Additional draws are cached for efficiency. The original repository suggests 2,048 additional samples as a practical starting point, potentially fewer for catalogs below 5–10K items; logQ correction does not apply to BPR-max. [Official sampler and masking](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py), [original implementation guidance](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).
